title: Playtesters kept saying my game felt floaty. It wasn't the jump physics
author: NewSpring2
selftext:
Making a small metroidvania in Godot. Claude handles most of the scripting. Had a few friends playtest last weekend and the same word kept coming up. Floaty.

So I pasted that into Claude and it did what every platformer guide says. Heavier fall gravity, less hang time at the top. Two evenings of that. It got tighter, but they still said floaty.

The actual fix was kind of embarrassing. The landing had no sound. The jump had a little whoosh and the landing was dead silent, so you never got that moment of hitting the ground. I added a thud and at the next playtest nobody said floaty. Didn't touch the physics again. (Added a dust puff later, but the sound did most of it.)

I made the thud in sonilo by just describing it and did a few takes. Redid the coin pickup while I was at it. Then I put the takes in an AudioStreamRandomizer with a bit of random pitch so the same thud doesn't play twice in a row. The whole thing took one evening.

Kind of humbling that two evenings of physics tweaks lost to one sound effect. Claude was never going to guess that one from the word floaty.

What's a tiny fix that changed how your game felt way more than it should have?

comments.author: Putrid_Clue_2127
comments.body: For my current game, which is an RTS hybrid on mobile, it was adding tracks on the ground after units walked over somewhere. For some reason it made a huge difference in making it feel like the units were part of the map itself

replies.author: NewSpring2
replies.body: very cool. do they fade out after a while or stick around the whole match? i got off easy with a sound, tracks feel like they'd add up fast on mobile once there's a lot of units

replies.author: Putrid_Clue_2127
replies.body: They fade out after about 5 seconds. Thankfully tracks are just a shader draw, so it's actually fairly efficient on memory. The thing I'm struggling with right now is making sure my assets aren't too high poly or too highly detailed. That's what kills my performance lol. I just want things to look the best they can!

comments.author: Any-Blacksmith-2054
comments.body: That's because Claude cannot hear. I can't wait they add sound modality to Opus

replies.author: NewSpring2
replies.body: lol would love that. "the landing sounds weak" isn't something i can paste into it yet

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body: Floaty also means your controls are not tight, if there is a delay between the input and the action it feels floaty.

replies.author: NewSpring2
replies.body: yeah i think the silent landing was a version of that. the jump fired right on the press, but nothing told you when you'd landed, so it read as late even when it wasn't
